a subset of neurons in the human MTL are invariant for complex visual stimuli, such as faces or objects, but not for simple stimuli like letters or numbers.

neurons in the medial temporal lobe of the human brain are selectively activated by pictures of faces, animals and objects and that some of these neurons are also selectively activated by pictures that differ strikingly in their visual properties, such as the viewing angle, size, and position, or even by letters that spell the name of the person, landmark or object.
neurons in the MTL respond selectively to faces, objects or scenes and to different images of given individuals or landmarks.

the study of human visual perception, with particular emphasis on the study of the human medial temporal region.
the study of the neural correlates of visual object and face recognition in the human brain.
the question of how the human brain processes visual information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human brain has the ability to recognize a person, object or landmark from a variety of different images and that the neurons in the medial temporal lobe are involved in this process.
the MTL is a key structure for the representation of invariant visual representations in the human brain.
the human MTL neurons are invariant to the stimulus size, but not the stimulus position and the viewing angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the medial temporal lobe contains neurons with a remarkable degree of visual invariance.
we have found neurons in the human MTL that are selective for complex images and that show a high level of invariance across changes in metric properties of the visual input.
the human medial temporal lobes (MTL) are the neural substrate for visual recognition memory and the formation of visual long-term memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the human brain can represent complex visual objects in a highly invariant way, even when the stimulus is seen under different viewing conditions or when it is represented by a different modality, such as by a name.

invariant representations are already present at the level of single cells in the human brain, and they are not only present at the level that we have previously reported, which is in the medial temporal lobe, but they are also present at the level where we have recorded in the human cortex.
the human brain is able to represent visual information at a level of abstraction that is not yet reached by artificial intelligence systems.
